articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 488, Jill hosts an action‑packed Linux adventure with Zeb and special guest host **Mathieu Comandon**, creator of Lutris. Mathieu brings massive Linux gaming updates, including **Easy Anti‑Cheat Linux v2**, the **Epic Games Launcher AppImage Beta**, and his early impressions of the **Steam Frame** - marking one of the biggest Linux gaming leaps in years.

Jill announces upcoming **Destination Linux community game streams**, featuring Jackbox, Golf With Your Friends, Serious Sam, and more - all streamed on Twitch and the platform with the big red button.

Zeb covers three major news stories shaking the tech world:

- **Linus Torvalds using AI/LLMs** to decipher complex kernel patches

- A **Discord data breach** affecting millions

- Denmark’s unbelievable **“123456” password** incident exposing 88 million records

Jill wraps up with a deep dive into **F‑Droid 2.0**, the largest overhaul of the privacy‑centric Android app store in nearly a decade - featuring a modern UI, expanded search, automatic background updates, and Jetpack Compose redesign.

Plus, we highlight new Patrons, community feedback, and plenty of laughs along the way.

articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 487, Ryan hosts an episode packed with open‑source news, community stories, and the triumphant return of **Rocco**, bringing that classic Big Daddy Linux energy back to the show for the second time in a single month.

We kick things off with heartfelt community feedback from O.C. Supertoner, followed by a lively discussion about AI‑generated code and whether Linux users should embrace or reject LLM‑assisted development. Rocco shares his thoughts on the new Hylki email client for GNOME and the growing debate around AI contributions in open‑source projects.

Zeb covers the end of the Orion browser for Linux and the implications of Kagi open‑sourcing its codebase. He also dives into the Netherlands’ bold move to adopt a Nix‑based government desktop after sanctions disrupted ICC access to Microsoft services, plus Amazon blocking Meta’s AI shopping agent.

It’s a fun, fast‑moving episode full of laughs, insights, and the open‑source passion that makes Destination Linux feel like home.

articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 486, Jill hosts an extended and heartfelt conversation with **Monica Ayhens‑Madon**, one of the most passionate open‑source community advocates in the Linux world. Monica shares her journey from Canonical’s Community Team to Ubuntu MATE, her time on the Ubuntu Community Council, and her current role helping shape the future of Thunderbird.

We dive into the upcoming **Thundermail** web client, Thunderbird’s modernization efforts, community building, privacy, security, and the philosophy behind empowering users through open‑source tools. Ryan discusses data portability and rclone, Zeb brings his signature wit, and Jill leads the conversation with warmth and enthusiasm.

This episode ran long - in the best way - because the conversation with Monica was simply too good to cut short.

articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 485, Ryan, Jill, and Zeb are joined by **Craig from Sandfly Security** for a deep dive into the latest Linux security trends. Craig shares insights from the upcoming Cold Incident Response Conference, including modern Linux malware tactics, IoT rootkit risks, fake kernel threads, UPX‑packed binaries, and new Golang C2 frameworks targeting non‑x86 platforms.

Jill highlights major updates in OpenRGB, including expanded support for GPUs, keyboards, motherboards, and more. Zeb covers Peppermint OS shifting from X.Org to XLibre, Ubuntu 26.10 unexpectedly adopting the Linux 7.3 kernel, and MX Linux’s forum being hit with a massive DDoS attack. Plus community feedback, Sandfly Security, and closing thoughts from the DL crew.

In Destination Linux Episode 482, Jill leads a very special show featuring the long‑awaited return of a very special creator, one of the original hosts who helped build Destination Linux from the ground up. It’s been years since he last joined us, and we’re thrilled to have him back.

We also welcome Red Hat VP Mike McGrath for an in‑depth conversation about Lightwell - a new approach to simplifying modern infrastructure, improving predictability, and supporting open source ecosystems at scale. Mike shares insights on AI’s rapid rise, open source economics, partnerships with industry heavyweights, and how Lightwell helps developers, sysadmins, and researchers in real‑world environments.

Along the way, we cover Session chat updates, website security improvements, and reflect on the origins of Destination Linux with Rocco. We wrap with a fun lightning round.

We explore the realities of surveillance, motion‑sensing routers with privacy tradeoffs, and Cr
articles.content:
Welcome to Destination Linux Episode 481. Ryan and Jill are joined by returning guest host Craig Rowland, founder and CEO of Sandfly Security, for a deep dive into the latest security, AI, and Linux news.

We explore the realities of surveillance, motion‑sensing routers with privacy tradeoffs, and Craig’s full breakdown of the chaos and hype coming out of Black Hat - including agentic AI, guardrails that don’t guard anything, and the growing divide between restricted AI and open‑weight models. Craig also covers the Cold Incident Response Conference, AI‑powered threat detection, and a Bitcoin RNG hack that proves why dice still matter.

Jill celebrates Linux’s 35th birthday and Valve’s 30th anniversary with a look back at the milestones that shaped open source, gaming, and the Linux desktop.
